question: Can the fixed canonical root reach an external NE port of its first whole-octahedron support through existing NN-phase-advance and neutron reader-phase-advance, without changing marks, requiring reference-P occupation or inventing a whole-body species law?
inputs: Unchanged GenerativeAssemblyRules; canonical marked P seed; actual PN target and its owner octahedron.
procedure: Generate native N-reader charts reached by NN and N-reader phase advances; retain paths, full five-slot maps and context provenance.
Record all reachable port faces relative to the original whole support; distinguish internal E components from external targets.
Do not identify absolute histories merely because chart geometry repeats. A finite chart quotient needs an explicit source-derived translation/invariance justification.
If no exit is found, distinguish bounded failure from a genuine invariant of the admitted N-only rules. Retain inverse-PN and root rebindings as excluded routes, not disproved possibilities.
successCriterion: Exhibit an actual fixed-root native continuation with an NE face on the original octahedron boundary and an external E primitive, with all native maps and occurrence witnesses validated.
failureCriterion: A validated finite quotient plus a source-derived invariant rules out such a port under exactly the specified N-only continuation rules; otherwise report only bounded non-discovery.
excludedClaims: reference geometry counts as constructed P
four constituent N readers count as one physical neutron
deliverable: Native reader atlas, explicit exit or scope-bounded obstruction, provenance and full-map controls.
